memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'"The fire on the altar must be kept burning; it must not go out. Every morning the priest is to add firewood and arrange the burnt offering on the fire and burn the fat of the fellowship offerings on it."'" - Lev 6:12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The fire kept burning on its own through the night. But every morning, someone had to add wood.

Both halves are true. God's provision was constant, and human faithfulness was required daily.

That balance saves us from two errors. The first is thinking everything depends on us — that if we slack off, God's work collapses. It does not. The fire burned all night without a single priest awake.

The second is thinking nothing depends on us — that since grace is free, effort is unnecessary. But the wood did not carry itself. Someone got up in the dark, gathered fuel, and tended what God had lit.

Paul held both together in one sentence: continue to work out your salvation with fear and trembling, for it is God who works in you (Phil 2:12-13). God works; therefore you work.

Notice the word every morning. Not when convenient, not when inspired. Daily, unremarkable faithfulness. The Christian life is built far more on ordinary consistency than on dramatic breakthroughs.

His compassions never fail. They are new every morning (Lam 3:22-23). God shows up every morning. The question is whether we do.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I depending entirely on inspiration rather than daily faithfulness?
2. What small daily practice could I begin — or return to — this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You keep the fire burning and You call me to bring the wood. Give me grace for ordinary, daily faithfulness. Amen.
